plan.chapter_thesis: Metasurface holography extends beyond display applications into computational imaging, metalens-based microscopy, beam steering, and optical computing, where distinct performance priorities reveal new dimensions of the mechanism-coupling problem.
plan.reader_takeaway: Different application domains (imaging, LiDAR, computing) impose unique constraints on resolution, field of view, and channel count, requiring tailored inverse design strategies that couple physical mechanisms with algorithmic reconstruction.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the foundational role of inverse design methods in enabling complex metasurfaces for non-display applications.
Detail advanced hybrid and physics-informed algorithms that improve generalization and efficiency in design.
Explain how computational reconstruction compensates for metasurface aberrations in imaging systems.
Describe specific high-throughput imaging applications like ptychography and temperature mapping.
Analyze multifunctional designs enabling multi-channel control for complex imaging tasks.
Transition to optical computing architectures leveraging metasurfaces for signal processing.
Address beam steering and sensing applications requiring precise wavefront collimation.
Synthesize current challenges in scaling design methodologies for diverse application spaces.

terminology_rows.note: Optimization process determining nanostructure geometry from desired optical response.
Imaging technique combining optical encoding with algorithmic reconstruction.
Flat optical element using subwavelength structures to focus light.
AI approach embedding physical laws into loss functions to constrain solutions.
Using light propagation through metasurfaces to perform mathematical operations.

explanation_block_rows.title: Foundations of Inverse Design for Advanced Applications
explanation_block_rows.goal: Define inverse design and establish its necessity for moving beyond simple display patterns to complex imaging functions.

explanation_block_rows.title: Hybrid and Physics-Constrained Algorithms
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain how hybrid neural-traditional optimizers and physics-informed losses overcome data scarcity and ensure physical realizability.

explanation_block_rows.title: Computational Correction in Metalens Imaging
explanation_block_rows.goal: Demonstrate how algorithmic reconstruction compensates for inherent chromatic and monochromatic aberrations in flat optics.

explanation_block_rows.title: Specialized Imaging: Ptychography and Thermography
explanation_block_rows.goal: Illustrate specific high-value applications where end-to-end co-design enables direct mapping of physical quantities.

explanation_block_rows.title: Multifunctionality and Channel Multiplexing
explanation_block_rows.goal: Show how deep learning enables independent control of spin, frequency, and phase for multi-channel holographic imaging.

explanation_block_rows.title: Metasurfaces for Optical Computing Architectures
explanation_block_rows.goal: Connect metasurface wavefront control to matrix multiplication and Fourier processing tasks in optical neural networks.

explanation_block_rows.title: Beam Steering and Resonant Sensing Mechanisms
explanation_block_rows.goal: Detail applications in LiDAR and sensing that rely on quasi-BIC resonances and precise beam collimation.

explanation_block_rows.title: Scaling Challenges and Future Methodologies
explanation_block_rows.goal: Summarize the trade-offs between computational cost and global optimality in large design spaces, pointing to foundation models.
